question: The ratio of incomes of Seema and Darshan is 4 : 3. They save ₹15,000 and ₹9,000, respectively. If the ratio of their expenditures is 16 : 17, then what is the total expenditure (in ₹) of Seema and Darshan?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Income ratio = 4 : 3 | Expenditure ratio = 16 : 17 | Savings = ₹15,000 & ₹9,000

Applying cross-multiplication: (4 × 17) − (3 × 16) = 20 units

Value difference = (17 × 15000) − (16 × 9000) = 255000 − 144000 = 111000

20 units = 111000 ⇒ 1 unit = 5550

Total Expenditure = Total Income − Total Savings = 7(5550) − 24000 = 14850

**∴ The correct answer is ₹14,850.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of incomes of Seema and Darshan = 4 : 3

Savings of Seema = ₹15,000 and Savings of Darshan = ₹9,000

Ratio of their expenditures = 16 : 17

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings ⇒ Expenditure = Income − Savings
